correctness.rationale: Exact factorization in X=T+T^{-1} proves positivity for r>=1/3 as a convolution of positive geometric Green kernels. For r<1/3 the decaying characteristic roots are nonreal conjugates, so the real kernel is a nonzero damped cosine sequence and must take negative values. Preservation of constants gives kernel mass one in the positive regime. The bundled checker verifies the algebra and a robust subthreshold witness without substituting finite computation for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The five-point stencil and general pentadiagonal inverse technology are prior. The checked literature did not state the sharp infinite-lattice backward Euler positivity threshold r=1/3. A highly relevant full text treats a different Q2-derived fourth-order discretization and obtains a lower time-step constraint, so the accepted claim is narrowed to the classical translation-invariant five-point stencil. The inaccessible full text of a 2015 pentadiagonal inverse paper is retained as the principal residual risk.

value.rationale: The result gives a sharp and structurally explained positivity boundary for a textbook fourth-order spatial stencil. It clarifies the counterintuitive fact that backward Euler can require a lower, rather than upper, step-size threshold to recover a discrete maximum principle, and it separates this classical long stencil from specially designed high-order monotone operators.
